title: The Sharp Ghost Again
premise: Coral Almeida, a deniable fixer for the Meridian Section—an embassy that exists on no map—receives a call on a burner phone he buried years ago, and the voice belongs to Ilse Varga, his former handler who officially died in a Vienna safehouse fire. She warns that an attack staged as an industrial accident will kill dozens at a Geneva summit, and that the order to let it happen came from inside Meridian itself. As Coral hunts the plotters while dodging his own colleagues, he uncovers that Ilse faked her death to escape the Section's corruption and that the attack is designed to justify Meridian's expansion into full black-ops autonomy. In the end, Coral chooses love and conscience over duty: he exposes the plot publicly, burns the Section's archives, and walks away with Ilse—invisible at last by choice rather than by orders.
about_author: Rosalind Pemberton is the pen name of a former diplomatic security consultant who spent a decade in cities that appear on no itineraries. She writes thrillers about people whose loyalties are their most dangerous possessions.

chapters.title: The Phone That Was Buried
chapters.summary: Coral Almeida's POV. Living quietly in Lisbon under a new identity, Coral receives a call on a burner phone he personally destroyed components of years ago. The voice is unmistakably Ilse Varga, dead for six years. She gives him thirty seconds of coordinates before the line dies. Emotional beat: dread and longing colliding—the past he mourned is calling collect.

chapters.title: Rules Written in Pencil
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. He reports nothing and flies to Vienna, where he finds the safehouse ruins freshly disturbed and evidence someone has been living there. Meanwhile, his current handler, Brandt, summons him with rewritten protocols that erase his own history from Section files. Emotional beat: the vertigo of realizing the institution rewriting rules is also erasing him.

chapters.title: A Woman Made of Ash
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Flashback interleaved with present: how she discovered Meridian planned the Vienna fire to silence her audit, how she survived, and why she chose Coral as the only person worth trusting. Present-day Ilse watches Coral arrive in Vienna, torn between using him and protecting him. Emotional beat: guilt sharpened into resolve.

chapters.title: The Accident Calendar
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Following Ilse's coordinates, Coral retrieves her hidden audit file revealing 'Operation Soft Landing'—an engineered catastrophe timed to the Geneva summit, designed to look like a gas main failure. He realizes Meridian's own logistics arm supplied the materials. Emotional beat: cold clarity; the enemy wears his own badge.

chapters.title: Brandt's Smile
chapters.summary: Brandt's POV. Brandt suspects Coral's unauthorized trip and begins closing the net, deploying a cleanup team led by the ruthless operative Sable. We see Brandt's genuine belief that one controlled tragedy will save thousands by expanding Meridian's mandate. Emotional beat: chilling sincerity—corruption wearing the mask of duty.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Invisible
chapters.summary: Coral and Ilse's POV alternating. Reunited in a Trieste safe flat, they argue about whether to go through channels or burn everything. Old love resurfaces alongside old wounds—he never knew why she vanished; she never forgave herself for what her survival cost. Emotional beat: tenderness negotiated between two people trained to lie.

chapters.title: Sable Comes Calling
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Sable's team ambushes them in Trieste; a brutal chase through the old port ends with Ilse captured and Coral wounded, escaping only because Sable wants him followed to any accomplices. Emotional beat: rage and helplessness—the cost of letting himself be known.

chapters.title: The Summit Ledger
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV, captive. Interrogated by Brandt, Ilse stalls by feeding him partial truths while memorizing the operational timeline she once built: the strike window opens in forty hours. Coral, tracking the cleanup team, finds her dead-drop backup proving the target is the summit's energy pavilion. Emotional beat: defiance under pressure; time bleeding out.

chapters.title: Soft Landing
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Climax at Geneva: Coral turns Sable by exposing that Brandt plans to eliminate the whole strike team afterward, then infiltrates the pavilion to disarm the staged gas system with minutes to spare while broadcasting the audit file to every delegate's terminal. Brandt is arrested by the very delegates he meant to weaponize. Emotional beat: breathless triumph shadowed by everything already lost.

chapters.title: The Sharp Ghost, Retired
chapters.summary: Coral and Ilse's POV together. With Meridian formally dissolved and both of them legally ghosts, Coral declines reinstatement offers and deletes his own file—the last act of obedience he'll ever perform. On a slow ferry out of Genoa, he and Ilse choose names, not codenames. Emotional beat: quiet peace; invisibility finally chosen, not imposed.
